discussion_comments.comment_body: The correct backward compatibility would be `basename(name || path)`, should I do that instead? The difference is if someone gave a path instead of a filename in the `filename` parameter.

Allowing `opts.expires` to be of type `number` breaks the consistency, that in all other cases `expires` is of type `Date`. This is also enfored by the TS' type defintion `@types/express` as defined [here](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/types/express-serve-static-core/index.d.ts#L349).

Based on my comment on https://github.com/expressjs/express/issues/5150#issuecomment-1496380734, I would propose to remove ~`opts.expires = new Date(Date.now() + maxAge)`~ entirely. Developers can still set this value as part of the function call. The maintainers will need to decide if this would be a breaking-change.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Also `200.0000000000000001 === 200` and `JSON.stringify(200.0000000000000001) === '200'`

Since JS sees this as 200, I dont think its worth the effort to differentiate it. Node's http module will turn it to 200 before it goes over the wire but also `200.05 => 200` which is really the behavior we are interested in.

``` js
var obj = [
  { href: 'http://foo' }
]

res.links(obj)

console.dir(obj) // <- the obj is now altered, which is not expected, especially if one wanted to just re-use the same object
```

There are two valid parameters for this function, an object like:

``` javascript
{
    next: 'http://api.example.com/users?page=2',
    last: 'http://api.example.com/users?page=5'
}
```

Which generates a link like this
`<http://api.example.com/users?page=2>; rel="next", <http://api.example.com/users?page=5>; rel="last", <http://api.example.com/users?page=1>; rel="prev"`

That's the implementation you see on line 106 and kept that way for backwards compatibility

This one is for the array parameter, which lets the user enter fine tune the links header.
What we can do here is to make no assumptions about the attribute value and let the user define the attributes like this:

``` javascript
{
    href: '"http://api.example.com/users?page=2"', // Quoted string
    rel: '"next"', // Quoted string
    hreflang: 'en' // Not quoted
}
```

Generating something like this:

`<http://api.example.com/users?page=2>; rel="next"; hreflang=en`

Thoughts?

Should probably use `res.send()` instead of `res.end()`.

`res.send()` will set the `Content-Type` header, remove unused headers, and maintain the same behavior as `res.send(status)`.

> The resulting sent text would be invalid html, this is not a good way to do it haha.

I'm not suggesting you do this, but we didn't prevent before, so I don't think preventing it now is going to help anyone. Do you think forcing the Content-Type to text is going to help people that do `res.type('html').sendStatus(500)`? I'm not against this... just don't see the point in forcing an opinion here.

> (also it doesn't need to return itself because it is an endpoint)

I agree that there isn't a practical reason to return itself but to be consistent it probably should. Eg. `send()` [returns itself](https://github.com/strongloop/express/blob/master/lib/response.js#L192).

maybe we can just make this a getter with a deprecation notice and return a noop as well as remove "docs" on it. it would make it more obvious that it's deprecated.
